newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai rubber prices ease in week on slack demand.
newsitem.headline: Thai rubber prices ease in week on slack demand.

text.p: Slow demand and rising supply continued to pressure prices on the Thai rubber market this week, trade sources said on Friday.

Rubber supplies entering the market rose by almost 40 percent this week compared with last week, according to auction market sources, and industry sources said they do not expect demand to pick up substantially anytime soon.

"The prices are likely to move around this range or lower until the end of this year. The news of the surplus and high stocks will continue to dent demand," said Sucharit Promdej, an advisor to the Rubber Research Center of Hat Yai.
Normally, buyers would buy the product at the end of the year to cover demand during March-April and prices usually rise due to a drop in supply.
"Buyers are not under pressure to buy as they anticipate that the surplus will continue in 1997," he said.

Heavy rainstorms, which have threatened rubber supplies on the east coast of southern Thailand, have barely have any impact on prices at the moment as rubber production from other drier areas are currently giving higher yields, market sources said.
Thai benchmark RSS3 for January shipment was quoted at $1.23-1.24 FOB Bangkok on Friday compared with around $1.25 earlier this week
STR20 for the same shipment was quoted around the same prices, traders said.
The latex price also eased slightly to 93 US cents from about 95 cents last week.
